model_info.name: Enzyme Competition - G6P Branch Point
model_info.description: Multiple enzymes competing for the same substrate (G6P) demonstrating race firing policy and test arc semantics
novel_features: Race firing policy for kinetic competition

initial_conditions.description: Normal cellular conditions with moderate G6P availability

P1_G6P.name: Glucose-6-Phosphate
P1_G6P.description: Central metabolite at critical branch point

P2_PFK_enzyme.name: Phosphofructokinase
P2_PFK_enzyme.description: Enzyme catalyst for glycolysis pathway (connected via test arc)

P3_G6PDH_enzyme.name: Glucose-6-Phosphate Dehydrogenase
P3_G6PDH_enzyme.description: Enzyme catalyst for pentose phosphate pathway (connected via test arc)

P6_ATP.name: Adenosine Triphosphate
P6_ATP.description: Energy currency, inhibits PFK when high (negative feedback)

P7_NADPH.name: Nicotinamide Adenine Dinucleotide Phosphate (reduced)
P7_NADPH.description: Reducing power, inhibits G6PDH when high (product inhibition)

T1_PFK.name: Phosphofructokinase Reaction
T1_PFK.label: PFK
T1_PFK.description: Commits G6P to glycolytic pathway with ATP inhibition

enzyme.name: Phosphofructokinase
enzyme.regulation: Allosteric: activated by AMP, ADP, F-2,6-BP; inhibited by ATP, citrate

T2_G6PDH.name: Glucose-6-Phosphate Dehydrogenase Reaction
T2_G6PDH.label: G6PDH
T2_G6PDH.description: First committed step of pentose phosphate pathway with NADPH inhibition

enzyme.name: Glucose-6-Phosphate Dehydrogenase
enzyme.clinical_relevance: Deficiency causes hemolytic anemia (most common enzyme deficiency)
enzyme.regulation: Product inhibition by NADPH, activated by NADP+

kinetics.reference: Marks PA et al. (1961) J. Biol. Chem. 236:1238-1240

A3_G6P_to_G6PDH.description: Substrate consumption by pentose phosphate pathway

A4_G6PDH_to_6PGL.description: Product formation from pentose phosphate pathway

A5_G6PDH_to_NADPH.description: NADPH production from pentose phosphate pathway

test_arcs.description: Non-consuming arcs for enzyme catalysts (Novel Feature!)

TA1_PFK_enzyme_to_PFK.description: Enzyme enables glycolysis but is NOT consumed
TA1_PFK_enzyme_to_PFK.biological_interpretation: Catalyst behavior - enzyme participates but remains available

TA2_G6PDH_enzyme_to_G6PDH.description: Enzyme enables pentose phosphate but is NOT consumed
TA2_G6PDH_enzyme_to_G6PDH.biological_interpretation: Catalyst behavior - enzyme participates but remains available

inhibitor_arcs.description: Inhibitor arcs for negative feedback regulation

I1_ATP_inhibits_PFK.biological_interpretation: When energy is abundant, slow down ATP production

I2_NADPH_inhibits_G6PDH.description: High NADPH inhibits pentose phosphate (product inhibition)
I2_NADPH_inhibits_G6PDH.biological_interpretation: When reducing power is abundant, slow down NADPH production

firing_policy.description: Mass action kinetics - transitions compete based on rates
firing_policy.algorithm: For each enabled transition, sample delay ~ Exp(rate); fire transition with minimum delay
firing_policy.biological_interpretation: Faster enzymes (higher Vmax) dominate flux distribution

comparison.race_vs_priority: Race: stochastic competition, Priority: deterministic hierarchy
comparison.biological_realism: Race policy matches actual molecular competition (Gillespie algorithm)

phase_1_initial.description: Rapid G6P consumption by both pathways

phase_2_competition.observation: Each G6P molecule consumed by PFK or G6PDH based on rate-weighted probability
phase_2_competition.verification: Plot F6P/6PGL ratio, should reflect enzyme Vmax ratio
phase_2_competition.key_insight: Race policy creates realistic flux distribution

phase_3_regulation.NADPH_effect: Accumulates, inhibits G6PDH when >200 μM, shifts flux to glycolysis
phase_3_regulation.ATP_effect: If accumulates >5 mM, inhibits PFK, shifts flux to pentose phosphate
phase_3_regulation.dynamic_balance: System self-regulates based on cofactor needs

test_arc_verification.fail_condition: If enzyme concentrations decrease, test arcs not implemented correctly

flux_partitioning.calculation: Ratio reflects Vmax_PFK/Vmax_G6PDH and enzyme concentrations

feedback_regulation.test: Monitor 6PGL production rate when NADPH >200 μM
feedback_regulation.expected: G6PDH rate decreases, more G6P goes to glycolysis

policy_comparison.experiment: Run with race vs random vs priority policies
policy_comparison.conclusion: Policy choice dramatically affects metabolic flux

G6PDH_deficiency.prevalence: 400+ million people worldwide (most common enzyme deficiency)
G6PDH_deficiency.cause: Mutations in G6PD gene reduce enzyme activity
G6PDH_deficiency.biochemical_effect: Reduced pentose phosphate flux, NADPH deficiency
G6PDH_deficiency.clinical_manifestation: Hemolytic anemia triggered by oxidative stress
G6PDH_deficiency.model_prediction: Reduce P3_G6PDH_enzyme to 0.5 μM, observe decreased 6PGL and NADPH production
G6PDH_deficiency.treatment: Avoid oxidative triggers (fava beans, certain drugs)
G6PDH_deficiency.oxidative_stress: Red blood cells cannot regenerate NADPH for glutathione reduction

cancer_metabolism.observation: Warburg effect - increased glycolysis despite oxygen availability
cancer_metabolism.mechanism: Upregulation of glycolytic enzymes AND pentose phosphate pathway
cancer_metabolism.model_simulation: Increase both PFK_enzyme and G6PDH_enzyme to 20 μM each
cancer_metabolism.purpose: ATP for proliferation + NADPH for biosynthesis + ribose-5-P for nucleotides
cancer_metabolism.therapeutic_target: G6PDH inhibitors under investigation for cancer therapy
cancer_metabolism.metabolic_reprogramming: Both pathways enhanced to support rapid cell division

diabetes.hyperglycemia: Elevated glucose leads to elevated G6P
diabetes.oxidative_stress: Excess NADPH production contributes to complications
diabetes.model_simulation: Increase initial G6P to 500 μM, observe product inhibition importance
diabetes.complications: Retinopathy, neuropathy, nephropathy linked to altered glucose metabolism

petri_net_concepts: Firing policies (race vs random vs priority)

detailed_analysis.description: High-resolution time course for publication-quality results

model_assumptions: Enzyme concentrations constant (justified by test arc semantics)
NADP+ concentration assumed constant (cofactor pool maintained)
ATP concentration decreases slowly (glycolysis consumes, but production not modeled here)
No explicit ATP synthesis included (focus on branch point only)
Products (F6P, 6PGL) do not feed back into G6P pool (open system)
extensions: Add ATP regeneration from downstream glycolysis
Include NADP+ as explicit place with NADPH/NADP+ cycling
Add F-2,6-BP as PFK activator (allosteric regulation)
Model oxidative stress by adding NADPH consumption reaction
computational_notes: Each firing event samples exponential delays
Large dt may miss fast dynamics
For publication quality, use dt=0.01 or smaller
